ES.news_1_full:
El pasado 22 de mayo de 2026, Bogotá alcanzó un hito histórico en su desarrollo urbano: el Tren número 2 de la Primera Línea del Metro completó su primera prueba de rodaje sobre el viaducto construido en el tramo sur-occidental de la ciudad. El recorrido, que cubrió los 14 kilómetros de viaducto ya terminados entre el Patio Taller de Bosa y la Estación 2 (Av. Villavicencio), fue supervisado por ingenieros del consorcio APCA Metro Línea 1 y técnicos de la firma china CRRC, fabricante del material rodante.

La prueba incluyó la verificación de sistemas de tracción, frenado regenerativo y señalización CBTC (Communication-Based Train Control), confirmando que los trenes pueden operar a velocidades de hasta 80 km/h en tramos rectos del viaducto. Con este avance, el proyecto alcanza un 77.53% de progreso general según el último corte oficial.

El tren, compuesto por 6 coches articulados con capacidad para 1,800 pasajeros, fue remolcado desde el Patio Taller donde se ensamblan las 30 unidades que conformarán la flota inicial. Este centro de mantenimiento, ubicado en la localidad de Bosa, tiene un avance del 91% y ya cuenta con las instalaciones de diagnóstico y talleres de revisión mayor.

La Empresa Metro de Bogotá (EMB) confirmó que las pruebas dinámicas continuarán durante el segundo semestre de 2026, con el objetivo de iniciar pruebas con pasajeros en 2027 y la apertura comercial de la línea en 2028. La inversión total del proyecto supera los 16 billones de pesos colombianos, financiados con recursos de la Nación, el Distrito y banca multilateral (BID, CAF, BEI, BIRF).
ES.news_2_full:
La construcción de la Primera Línea del Metro de Bogotá ha transformado significativamente la movilidad sobre la Avenida Caracas, uno de los corredores viales más importantes de la ciudad. Desde el inicio de las obras de cimentación profunda y pilotaje del viaducto, la avenida ha experimentado cierres parciales y totales en tramos estratégicos entre la Calle 1 y la Calle 72.

El Plan de Manejo de Tráfico (PMT) implementado por la Secretaría Distrital de Movilidad contempla desvíos por la Carrera 10, la NQS (Avenida Carrera 30) y rutas alternas por las Carreras 7 y 13. Sin embargo, los tiempos de desplazamiento en hora pico se han incrementado entre un 25% y un 40% según datos del Centro de Gestión de Tránsito de Bogotá.

Las obras más críticas se concentran actualmente en los tramos de la Calle 26 (donde se demolió la estación de TransMilenio), la Calle 39 en el sector de Teusaquillo, y el Intercambiador de la Calle 72. En estos puntos, las piloteadoras y grúas de gran capacidad operan en jornadas de 24 horas para acelerar el avance del proyecto.

La Alcaldía Mayor ha reforzado el servicio de TransMilenio con rutas provisionales, buses alimentadores adicionales y ciclo-infraestructura temporal para mitigar el impacto sobre los ciudadanos. Se estima que una vez en operación, la Línea 1 del Metro transportará entre 800,000 y 1,000,000 de pasajeros diarios, reduciendo la congestión en un 30%.
ES.news_3_full: Comerciantes del corredor de la Avenida Caracas reportan variaciones en sus ingresos debido a los cerramientos viales por las obras del viaducto. La Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá y la Alcaldía activaron mesas de concertación económica para brindar incentivos fiscales y apoyo financiero a los locales afectados durante la fase de cimentación.

es.news_1_full:
El pasado 22 de mayo de 2026, Bogotá alcanzó un hito histórico en su desarrollo urbano: el Tren número 2 de la Primera Línea del Metro completó su primera prueba de rodaje sobre el viaducto construido en el tramo sur-occidental de la ciudad. El recorrido, que cubrió los 14 kilómetros de viaducto ya terminados entre el Patio Taller de Bosa y la Estación 2 (Av. Villavicencio), fue supervisado por ingenieros del consorcio APCA Metro Línea 1 y técnicos de la firma china CRRC, fabricante del material rodante.

La prueba incluyó la verificación de sistemas de tracción, frenado regenerativo y señalización CBTC (Communication-Based Train Control), confirmando que los trenes pueden operar a velocidades de hasta 80 km/h en tramos rectos del viaducto. Con este avance, el proyecto alcanza un 77.53% de progreso general según el último corte oficial.

El tren, compuesto por 6 coches articulados con capacidad para 1,800 pasajeros, fue remolcado desde el Patio Taller donde se ensamblan las 30 unidades que conformarán la flota inicial. Este centro de mantenimiento, ubicado en la localidad de Bosa, tiene un avance del 91% y ya cuenta con las instalaciones de diagnóstico y talleres de revisión mayor.

La Empresa Metro de Bogotá (EMB) confirmó que las pruebas dinámicas continuarán durante el segundo semestre de 2026, con el objetivo de iniciar pruebas con pasajeros en 2027 y la apertura comercial de la línea en 2028. La inversión total del proyecto supera los 16 billones de pesos colombianos, financiados con recursos de la Nación, el Distrito y banca multilateral (BID, CAF, BEI, BIRF).
es.news_2_full:
La construcción de la Primera Línea del Metro de Bogotá ha transformado significativamente la movilidad sobre la Avenida Caracas, uno de los corredores viales más importantes de la ciudad. Desde el inicio de las obras de cimentación profunda y pilotaje del viaducto, la avenida ha experimentado cierres parciales y totales en tramos estratégicos entre la Calle 1 y la Calle 72.

El Plan de Manejo de Tráfico (PMT) implementado por la Secretaría Distrital de Movilidad contempla desvíos por la Carrera 10, la NQS (Avenida Carrera 30) y rutas alternas por las Carreras 7 y 13. Sin embargo, los tiempos de desplazamiento en hora pico se han incrementado entre un 25% y un 40% según datos del Centro de Gestión de Tránsito de Bogotá.

Las obras más críticas se concentran actualmente en los tramos de la Calle 26 (donde se demolió la estación de TransMilenio), la Calle 39 en el sector de Teusaquillo, y el Intercambiador de la Calle 72. En estos puntos, las piloteadoras y grúas de gran capacidad operan en jornadas de 24 horas para acelerar el avance del proyecto.

La Alcaldía Mayor ha reforzado el servicio de TransMilenio con rutas provisionales, buses alimentadores adicionales y ciclo-infraestructura temporal para mitigar el impacto sobre los ciudadanos. Se estima que una vez en operación, la Línea 1 del Metro transportará entre 800,000 y 1,000,000 de pasajeros diarios, reduciendo la congestión en un 30%.
es.news_3_full: Comerciantes del corredor de la Avenida Caracas reportan variaciones en sus ingresos debido a los cerramientos viales por las obras del viaducto. La Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá y la Alcaldía activaron mesas de concertación económica para brindar incentivos fiscales y apoyo financiero a los locales afectados durante la fase de cimentación.

EN.news_1_full:
On May 22, 2026, Bogotá reached a historic milestone in its urban development: Train number 2 of the First Metro Line completed its first rolling test on the viaduct built in the southwestern section of the city. The route, which covered the 14 kilometers of viaduct already completed between the Bosa Workshop Yard and Station 2 (Av. Villavicencio), was supervised by engineers from the APCA Metro Línea 1 consortium and technicians from the Chinese firm CRRC, manufacturer of the rolling stock.

The test included the verification of traction systems, regenerative braking, and CBTC (Communication-Based Train Control) signaling, confirming that the trains can operate at speeds of up to 80 km/h on straight sections of the viaduct. With this advance, the project reaches 77.53% overall progress according to the latest official cutoff.

The train, consisting of 6 articulated cars with a capacity for 1,800 passengers, was towed from the Workshop Yard where the 30 units that will make up the initial fleet are assembled. This maintenance center, located in the Bosa locality, is 91% complete and already has diagnostic facilities and major overhaul workshops.

The Bogotá Metro Company (EMB) confirmed that dynamic tests will continue during the second half of 2026, with the goal of starting passenger tests in 2027 and the commercial opening of the line in 2028. The total investment of the project exceeds 16 trillion Colombian pesos, financed with resources from the Nation, the District, and multilateral banks (IDB, CAF, EIB, IBRD).
EN.news_2_full:
The construction of the First Line of the Bogotá Metro has significantly transformed mobility on Avenida Caracas, one of the most important road corridors in the city. Since the beginning of the deep foundation and piling works for the viaduct, the avenue has experienced partial and total closures in strategic sections between Calle 1 and Calle 72.

The Traffic Management Plan (PMT) implemented by the District Mobility Secretariat includes detours along Carrera 10, the NQS (Avenida Carrera 30), and alternate routes along Carreras 7 and 13. However, travel times during rush hour have increased between 25% and 40% according to data from the Bogotá Traffic Management Center.

The most critical works are currently concentrated in the sections of Calle 26 (where the TransMilenio station was demolished), Calle 39 in the Teusaquillo sector, and the Calle 72 Interchange. At these points, pile drivers and high-capacity cranes operate 24 hours a day to accelerate the project's progress.

The Mayor's Office has reinforced the TransMilenio service with provisional routes, additional feeder buses, and temporary cycling infrastructure to mitigate the impact on citizens. It is estimated that once in operation, Line 1 of the Metro will transport between 800,000 and 1,000,000 passengers daily, reducing congestion by 30%.
EN.news_3_full: Merchants along the Avenida Caracas corridor report fluctuations in income due to road closures for viaduct construction. The Bogotá Chamber of Commerce and the Mayor's Office activated economic dialogue tables to provide tax incentives and financial support to affected local businesses during the foundation phase.

en.news_1_full:
On May 22, 2026, Bogotá reached a historic milestone in its urban development: Train number 2 of the First Metro Line completed its first rolling test on the viaduct built in the southwestern section of the city. The route, which covered the 14 kilometers of viaduct already completed between the Bosa Workshop Yard and Station 2 (Av. Villavicencio), was supervised by engineers from the APCA Metro Línea 1 consortium and technicians from the Chinese firm CRRC, manufacturer of the rolling stock.

The test included the verification of traction systems, regenerative braking, and CBTC (Communication-Based Train Control) signaling, confirming that the trains can operate at speeds of up to 80 km/h on straight sections of the viaduct. With this advance, the project reaches 77.53% overall progress according to the latest official cutoff.

The train, consisting of 6 articulated cars with a capacity for 1,800 passengers, was towed from the Workshop Yard where the 30 units that will make up the initial fleet are assembled. This maintenance center, located in the Bosa locality, is 91% complete and already has diagnostic facilities and major overhaul workshops.

The Bogotá Metro Company (EMB) confirmed that dynamic tests will continue during the second half of 2026, with the goal of starting passenger tests in 2027 and the commercial opening of the line in 2028. The total investment of the project exceeds 16 trillion Colombian pesos, financed with resources from the Nation, the District, and multilateral banks (IDB, CAF, EIB, IBRD).
en.news_2_full:
The construction of the First Line of the Bogotá Metro has significantly transformed mobility on Avenida Caracas, one of the most important road corridors in the city. Since the beginning of the deep foundation and piling works for the viaduct, the avenue has experienced partial and total closures in strategic sections between Calle 1 and Calle 72.

The Traffic Management Plan (PMT) implemented by the District Mobility Secretariat includes detours along Carrera 10, the NQS (Avenida Carrera 30), and alternate routes along Carreras 7 and 13. However, travel times during rush hour have increased between 25% and 40% according to data from the Bogotá Traffic Management Center.

The most critical works are currently concentrated in the sections of Calle 26 (where the TransMilenio station was demolished), Calle 39 in the Teusaquillo sector, and the Calle 72 Interchange. At these points, pile drivers and high-capacity cranes operate 24 hours a day to accelerate the project's progress.

The Mayor's Office has reinforced the TransMilenio service with provisional routes, additional feeder buses, and temporary cycling infrastructure to mitigate the impact on citizens. It is estimated that once in operation, Line 1 of the Metro will transport between 800,000 and 1,000,000 passengers daily, reducing congestion by 30%.
en.news_3_full: Merchants along the Avenida Caracas corridor report fluctuations in income due to road closures for viaduct construction. The Bogotá Chamber of Commerce and the Mayor's Office activated economic dialogue tables to provide tax incentives and financial support to affected local businesses during the foundation phase.

pt.news_1_full:
On May 22, 2026, Bogotá reached a historic milestone in its urban development: Train number 2 of the First Metro Line completed its first rolling test on the viaduct built in the southwestern section of the city. The route, which covered the 14 kilometers of viaduct already completed between the Bosa Workshop Yard and Station 2 (Av. Villavicencio), was supervised by engineers from the APCA Metro Línea 1 consortium and technicians from the Chinese firm CRRC, manufacturer of the rolling stock.

The test included the verification of traction systems, regenerative braking, and CBTC (Communication-Based Train Control) signaling, confirming that the trains can operate at speeds of up to 80 km/h on straight sections of the viaduct. With this advance, the project reaches 77.53% overall progress according to the latest official cutoff.

The train, consisting of 6 articulated cars with a capacity for 1,800 passengers, was towed from the Workshop Yard where the 30 units that will make up the initial fleet are assembled. This maintenance center, located in the Bosa locality, is 91% complete and already has diagnostic facilities and major overhaul workshops.

The Bogotá Metro Company (EMB) confirmed that dynamic tests will continue during the second half of 2026, with the goal of starting passenger tests in 2027 and the commercial opening of the line in 2028. The total investment of the project exceeds 16 trillion Colombian pesos, financed with resources from the Nation, the District, and multilateral banks (IDB, CAF, EIB, IBRD).
pt.news_2_full:
The construction of the First Line of the Bogotá Metro has significantly transformed mobility on Avenida Caracas, one of the most important road corridors in the city. Since the beginning of the deep foundation and piling works for the viaduct, the avenue has experienced partial and total closures in strategic sections between Calle 1 and Calle 72.

The Traffic Management Plan (PMT) implemented by the District Mobility Secretariat includes detours along Carrera 10, the NQS (Avenida Carrera 30), and alternate routes along Carreras 7 and 13. However, travel times during rush hour have increased between 25% and 40% according to data from the Bogotá Traffic Management Center.

The most critical works are currently concentrated in the sections of Calle 26 (where the TransMilenio station was demolished), Calle 39 in the Teusaquillo sector, and the Calle 72 Interchange. At these points, pile drivers and high-capacity cranes operate 24 hours a day to accelerate the project's progress.

The Mayor's Office has reinforced the TransMilenio service with provisional routes, additional feeder buses, and temporary cycling infrastructure to mitigate the impact on citizens. It is estimated that once in operation, Line 1 of the Metro will transport between 800,000 and 1,000,000 passengers daily, reducing congestion by 30%.
pt.news_3_full: Merchants along the Avenida Caracas corridor report fluctuations in income due to road closures for viaduct construction. The Bogotá Chamber of Commerce and the Mayor's Office activated economic dialogue tables to provide tax incentives and financial support to affected local businesses during the foundation phase.

zh.news_1_full:
On May 22, 2026, Bogotá reached a historic milestone in its urban development: Train number 2 of the First Metro Line completed its first rolling test on the viaduct built in the southwestern section of the city. The route, which covered the 14 kilometers of viaduct already completed between the Bosa Workshop Yard and Station 2 (Av. Villavicencio), was supervised by engineers from the APCA Metro Línea 1 consortium and technicians from the Chinese firm CRRC, manufacturer of the rolling stock.

The test included the verification of traction systems, regenerative braking, and CBTC (Communication-Based Train Control) signaling, confirming that the trains can operate at speeds of up to 80 km/h on straight sections of the viaduct. With this advance, the project reaches 77.53% overall progress according to the latest official cutoff.

The train, consisting of 6 articulated cars with a capacity for 1,800 passengers, was towed from the Workshop Yard where the 30 units that will make up the initial fleet are assembled. This maintenance center, located in the Bosa locality, is 91% complete and already has diagnostic facilities and major overhaul workshops.

The Bogotá Metro Company (EMB) confirmed that dynamic tests will continue during the second half of 2026, with the goal of starting passenger tests in 2027 and the commercial opening of the line in 2028. The total investment of the project exceeds 16 trillion Colombian pesos, financed with resources from the Nation, the District, and multilateral banks (IDB, CAF, EIB, IBRD).
zh.news_2_full:
The construction of the First Line of the Bogotá Metro has significantly transformed mobility on Avenida Caracas, one of the most important road corridors in the city. Since the beginning of the deep foundation and piling works for the viaduct, the avenue has experienced partial and total closures in strategic sections between Calle 1 and Calle 72.

The Traffic Management Plan (PMT) implemented by the District Mobility Secretariat includes detours along Carrera 10, the NQS (Avenida Carrera 30), and alternate routes along Carreras 7 and 13. However, travel times during rush hour have increased between 25% and 40% according to data from the Bogotá Traffic Management Center.

The most critical works are currently concentrated in the sections of Calle 26 (where the TransMilenio station was demolished), Calle 39 in the Teusaquillo sector, and the Calle 72 Interchange. At these points, pile drivers and high-capacity cranes operate 24 hours a day to accelerate the project's progress.

The Mayor's Office has reinforced the TransMilenio service with provisional routes, additional feeder buses, and temporary cycling infrastructure to mitigate the impact on citizens. It is estimated that once in operation, Line 1 of the Metro will transport between 800,000 and 1,000,000 passengers daily, reducing congestion by 30%.
zh.news_3_full: Merchants along the Avenida Caracas corridor report fluctuations in income due to road closures for viaduct construction. The Bogotá Chamber of Commerce and the Mayor's Office activated economic dialogue tables to provide tax incentives and financial support to affected local businesses during the foundation phase.
